text: When you design a REST API, clear structure is important. Start by choosing simple, meaningful endpoints that describe your resources, such as /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods and return proper status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing. Good documentation helps other developers understand how to use your API quickly. It is also wise to use versioning, for example /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing clients. Finally, keep your responses consistent and easy to read, because a well-designed API saves time for everyone who works with it.
